title: Simulating Supply and Demand
subject: Economics
beats: Start with one buyer and one seller, build up to a full market, then argue about it
Blue blobs sell rockets, orange blobs buy
Each seller has a minimum price, each buyer a maximum
Concrete numbers: max $40, min $20, trade at $30; each gains $10
That gain is named surplus, a way to quantify slippery value
Add a second buyer with a slightly lower limit
Simulation rules: expected prices, random order, adjust after each day
Run with one buyer and one seller: nothing happens
Add the second buyer: what do you expect? Price creeps up
Competing buyers pay more; sellers get the surplus
Add two sellers (3 vs 2): what will happen?
Price falls; competing sellers hand surplus to buyers
Three buyers, three sellers: predict it
Too many blobs: reorganize the display into separate rows
Only two rockets sell: the lowest buyer and highest seller can never agree
Set the price high or low by hand and watch it settle
Equilibrium: where quantity supplied equals quantity demanded
For huge markets, draw supply and demand curves; they cross at equilibrium
Now the arguing; specifics vary, so only broad strokes
Equilibrium maximizes surplus; one more trade would be negative (not a rigorous proof)
Right number of participants: that's what efficient means; invisible hand
Is the ideal a good model? Needs many traders, free exit, good information
Is total surplus the right goal? Food, labor, healthcare
Markets are a tool, neither good nor bad
Joke: free educational videos are a confusing market; like and subscribe

meta.brute_force: yes 3:48: the 1-buyer-1-seller run where nothing happens, then add one blob at a time
meta.examples_grow: grows strictly in size, one agent at a time, then compresses to curves
